newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 8.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
- The Irish government is to throw down a direct election challenge to the opposition parties on water charges by publishing the legislation which would end them.

- Ireland's Frank McCourt raised a glass of champagne to Limerick and his brothers on Monday as he scooped the Pulitzer Prize, America's top literary award, for his biographical account of life in the city's slums during the 1930's and '40's.

- Ireland's Telecom Eireann is to cut the cost of phone calls and fixed charges by up to 80 million Irish pounds over the next year in the largest package of price reductions announced so far by the company.
- The Irish pound slumped to a near four-year low against sterling on Monday, as the British currency was lifted by another surge in the dollar.

- Economic growth and increased numbers at work in Ireland mean a basic income scheme for everyone could be implemented at less cost than had been thought, according to a new study published on Monday.

- The President of Ireland, Mary Robinson, is now considered likely to be appointed to the vacant post of United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, according to sources in Dublin, Geneva and New York.
- Ireland's Telecom Eireann has announced a wide range of price reductions which it says will save consumers a total of 80 million Irish pounds in a full year.
- New laws on the right of adopted people to see their birth records and to contact their natural parents are to be brought forwards as a priority by the Irish government.

- A renewed burst from sterling which gained almost four pfennigs versus the German mark on Monday to break through its former European exchange rate mechanism floor and reach its highest level since "Black Wednesday" in 1992, has pushed the Irish pound down towards 95 pence against sterling, its lowest level for over three years.
